Here is a comprehensive Application Design and Requirement Document (SRS) based exactly on your review. This document allows no ambiguity for developers and covers every single feature, design preference, and workflow logic you requested.

Application Design Document: Sales Executive Daily Reporting Tool
1. Project Overview

App Name: (Proposed: SalesTrack / BajajDaily)
Platform: Web Application (PWA - Progressive Web App) optimized for Mobile.
Primary User: Sales Executives (specifically detailed for appliance sales).
Goal: To enable sales executives to log daily sales, manage cumulative reports, track Monthly to Date (MTD) performance, manage customer complaints (CRM), and export detailed data.

2. UI/UX Design Specifications

The visual aesthetic is a strict requirement for this application.

Theme: iOS-style "Glassmorphism" (Glassy Theme). High transparency, background blur effects, and floating elements.

Responsiveness: Fully mobile-friendly. Elements must resize and stack perfectly on all screen sizes.

Modes:

Light Mode: Clean, crisp glass look.

Dark Mode: Deep visuals with neon/glass accents. (Must be toggleable).

Animations: "Soo smooth" transitions between tabs.

Loading Screen: A beautiful, aesthetic loading splash screen upon opening the app.

Images: All uploaded bill copies/images must be zoomable (pinch-to-zoom) and maintain high resolution (HD).

3. Navigation Structure

The app will utilize a fixed Bottom Navigation Bar with glass effect containing four tabs:

Dashboard

New Entry

CRM

Settings

4. Detailed Module Specifications
A. Authentication (Login)

Type: One-time Login (Persistent). Once logged in, the app remembers the user permanently until they manually log out or clear cache.

Input Fields:

Username

Employee ID (Compulsory)

Phone Number

Email (Optional)

Store Name/Location (e.g., RELIANCE DIGITAL JPNAGARA)

Constraint: Safe data entry (validation on phone numbers and email).

B. Module 1: Dashboard

This is the home screen. It must display two types of views (toggleable or stacked).

1. Top Section: Target & Achievement

Visual: A Progress Bar showing Monthly Target vs. Current Achievement.

Data: Updates dynamically based on the "MTD Sale Value."

2. View Type A: Calendar View

Visual: A monthly calendar grid.

Indicators:

Days with sales: Show the Total Quantity Sold number inside the date box.

Days with no sales/off: labeled as "Week Off" or "0".

Interaction: Clicking a Date opens a Detailed Pop-up/Modal:

List: Shows items sold that day, individual quantity, and individual price.

Bill Copy: Shows the uploaded bill image (Zoomable).

Action Button 1: "Save Bill to Gallery".

Action Button 2: "Copy Daily Report". (See Logic Section F for text format).

3. View Type B: List View

Visual: Vertical scrollable list of daily entries.

Functionality:

Edit: Allow user to modify Price and Quantity directly in the list.

Delete: Option to delete a specific individual report entry.

Bill View: Thumbnail of the bill (clickable to zoom).

C. Module 2: New Entry (The Core Workflow)

This section handles data input with specific cumulative logic.

Inputs:

Date Selection: Date Picker (Format: dd-mm-yyyy).

Product Selection: (Dropdown or Text Input).

Quantity: Numeric input.

Value (Price): Numeric currency input.

Bill Upload: Camera/Gallery upload for the specific product(s).

Multiple Items: The user can add multiple different products for the same date in one session.

The "Cumulative Logic" (Crucial):

Scenario:

User sells 2 Irons in the morning 
→
→
 Enters data 
→
→
 Generates Report.

User sells 2 Mixers in the evening 
→
→
 Selects same date 
→
→
 Enters new data.

Result: The system must append the new data to the old data.

Morning Report: 2 Irons.

Evening Report: 2 Irons + 2 Mixers.

MTD Calculation: Automatically updates total monthly value.

Post-Entry Actions:

Once submitted, the screen displays a summary:

Total Today's Value: (Calculated sum).

Total Today's Qty: (Calculated sum).

Action Button 1: Share via WhatsApp (Opens WhatsApp with the formatted text).

Action Button 2: Copy to Clipboard.

D. Module 3: CRM (Customer Relationship Management)

A simple interface to track customer service issues.

Inputs:

Customer Name

Phone Number

Product Model

Issue Type: Installation / Complaint.

Status Toggle:

Resolved (Green)

Not Resolved (Red)

List View: History of all raised complaints.

E. Module 4: Settings & Profile

User Profile:

Edit Profile details (Name, Store, ID).

Profile Photo: Allow user to upload/change their photo.

Support:

WhatsApp Support: Button linking to +91 70399 20000.

Website: Link to https://www.bajajelectricals.com/.

Data Management (Import/Export):

Format 1: JSON (Full data backup).

Format 2: Excel (Columns: Date, Product, Quantity, Value).

Format 3: PDF (Sales Report + HD Bill Copies embedded in the PDF for proof).

5. Functional Logic & Calculations
F. Clipboard / WhatsApp Report Format

When the user clicks "Copy Report" or "Share", the text must generate exactly in this format (Dynamic values in brackets):

code
Text
download
content_copy
expand_less
Name: [User Name]
Date: [dd/mm/yy]
Store Location: [Store Name]

Today’s Sale Value: = [Total Daily Value]
Today’s Sale qty = [Total Daily Qty]

[Product A Name] Qty: = [Qty]
[Product B Name] Qty: = [Qty]
[Product C Name] Qty: = [Qty]
... (List continues for all items sold today)

MTD Sale Value = [Sum of ALL sales from 1st of month to today]
G. MTD (Month to Date) Calculation

Logic: Sum of "Total Sale Value" of every entry where the month matches the current month.

Display: Visible on Dashboard (Target Bar) and at the bottom of the text report.

6. Technical Requirements

Safety Constraints:

Price and Quantity fields must only accept numbers.

Date format must be strictly dd-mm-yyyy.

Prevent accidental deletion (add a "Are you sure?" confirmation on delete).

Performance:

App must be lightweight.

Transitions and scrolling must be smooth (60fps).

Storage:

Images needs to be compressed for storage but displayed in HD when zoomed.

Local storage/Database must handle persistent login state.

7. Developer Checklist (Summary)

iOS Glassy Theme & Dark Mode implemented?

Login: Username, Emp ID, Phone, Store (One-time save)?

Dashboard: Calendar View (Qty displayed) & List View?

Dashboard: Target vs Achievement Bar?

Entry: Cumulative logic (add to existing day's report)?

Report Format: Matches the "PRAJWAL" example exactly?

MTD: Automatically calculated and included in text report?

Bill Copies: Zoomable, Save to Gallery, Included in PDF export?

Export: JSON, Excel, PDF?

Support Links: WhatsApp (+917039920000) & URL active?

CRM: Complaint tracking with Status?

**Envisioning the Interface**

I'm now fully immersed in the UI/UX aspects, particularly the iOS Glassmorphism and the implementation of light/dark modes. Smooth animations are crucial, and I'm exploring potential frameworks for the splash screen. The overall navigation structure is solidifying: Dashboard, New Entry, CRM, and Settings are essential. Persistent login with name is a primary focus for auth.


**Outlining Core Features**

I've been meticulously defining the app's core functionalities. The Dashboard will feature target vs. achievement metrics and a calendar/list view for data visualization. "New Entry" will streamline sales input with image uploading and post-entry summaries.  I'm also outlining the CRM for complaint tracking and the Settings section for user customization and data export. React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS will be the cornerstone technologies.


**Planning the App Structure**

I'm deep into the architecture now. The file structure is taking shape, with `index.tsx` as the React root, `App.tsx` handling routing. I've got `types.ts` defined for core data and `constants.ts` with initial states. Components are organized: Layout with Glassmorphism and navigation, SplashScreen, Dashboard, NewEntry, CRM, Settings, and reusable Glassy UI components like Modal, Button, and Input. Services for storage and export are also starting to take form.


**Developing Implementation Details**

I'm now focusing on implementation. I've decided to leverage `useState` and `useEffect` with LocalStorage for streamlined state management. Data persistence seems feasible without Redux for this scope. I'm building cumulative logic for entries, checking for existing dates before appending data. I'll store images as Base64 strings, acknowledging potential size limits. For exporting, I'll prioritize CSV and JSON, with a fallback to `window.print()` for PDF-like functionality, given constraints. My library choices include `lucide-react` for icons, `recharts` for charts, and `framer-motion` for animations. I'm opting for native `Date` for date handling.


**Mapping Data Structures**

Now, I'm defining the application's data structures, focusing on crucial interface types such as `UserProfile`, `SaleItem`, `DailyReport`, and `Complaint`. I'm establishing helper functions within `storageService.ts` for localStorage operations, including retrieval, saving, and modification of user and sales data, as well as handling complaints. I'm strategizing how `App.tsx` will manage the overall routing and splash screen display. I'm outlining how the Dashboard will utilize a calendar grid and a simple progress bar, while the NewEntry component will handle form submissions and image uploads via `<input type="file">`.


**Organizing Core Components**

I'm structuring the `components/ui` folder to house reusable Glassy components like `Card`, `Button`, and `Input` for consistent styling.  I've refined the cumulative logic for sales, now using a `DailyReport[]` with individual `SaleItem` entries. When adding sales, it finds or creates a report for the specific date and updates the associated item list and totals. I'm also planning a helper function for text formatting to facilitate easy sharing via clipboard or WhatsApp. My implementation plan is broken down into Setup Types, Storage Service, UI Components, Feature Components, and App & Layout in order. I've realized client-side image compression might be tricky, but I will implement a canvas resizing to reduce the size of the base64 strings.


**Addressing PDF and Targets**

I'm tackling the "PDF Export" challenge by creating a print-optimized view as a workaround, avoiding complex client-side PDF generation. I'm also adding a "Monthly Target Value" field in the Settings to enable "Target vs. Achievement" visualization. My next focus is implementing a theme toggle using context or state for smooth dark/light mode switching. I'm finally ready to start coding!

**Investigating Image Compression**

I'm currently looking into the type error in `NewEntry.tsx`, specifically around the image compression logic on line 44. It seems the `compressImage` function is expecting a `File` object as input, but the data being passed is not recognized as such. I'm digging deeper into how the `files` array is populated and examining the data type of its elements to ensure compatibility with `compressImage`.


**Examining File Type Issues**

I've been meticulously examining the potential type mismatch causing the error around `e.target.files`. It appears the conversion using `Array.from` from `FileList` to `File[]` may be the culprit. I'm investigating why TypeScript might be inferring an `unknown` type, hindering the expected `File` object assignment to `compressImage`. Delving into the React event object's `target` and checking the properties it is exposing. I'm scrutinizing `FileList` and `File` object definitions.


**Debugging Type Inferences**

I'm now focusing on the specific cause of the type inference issue. It appears the environment might be causing `Array.from(e.target.files)` to infer `unknown[]` instead of `File[]`, even though `FileList` should iterate `File` objects. I've considered explicitly typing the variable or casting as a solution, as well as double-checking the `compressImage` function's argument type and ensuring it explicitly expects a `File`. My current focus is to see which of these approaches is more robust.


**Resolving FileList Typing**
